read_scope: Full handwritten C encoder, wrapper, CMake and new test source; original Python writer compared field by field. Prior batched candidate and fixture hashes bound, not new independent functional execution.
conclusions: Ordered local capture, extension, receipt, coverage and optional ACK traversal matches the original typed writer; no field omitted or reordered in the inspected implementation.

Exact dictionary keys are checked without supplied hashing or equality before lookup. Unsupported values/containers return NotImplemented without supplied hooks; only that marker invokes the original once. Encoding/resource exceptions propagate without fallback.

uint64 uses exact integer/bool modulo-2^64 semantics. Binary64 uses PyFloat_Pack8 in big endian; NaN/Inf/signed zero are not rejected. Exact integer doubles outside signed64 defer to original struct behavior.
Exact Unicode uses strict UTF8 at the original consumed text position; surrogate failures propagate. Unconsumed values and aliases are ignored or revisited as the original does.

Borrowed input references remain under the declared stable rooted input. New UTF8 references use RAII; module state retains interned keys; no input, observation or result cache and no simulator authority.

Draft functional tests cover complete bytes, all consumed scalar positions, errors/hooks, large integers, binary64 special values, Unicode and failure recovery; these tests have not been run by this reviewer.
limits: Source review is not compiled C acceptance, functional parity, performance evidence or capture authenticity.
CPython 3.11.9 and stable private input only. Allocation, signal/interrupt and concurrent mutation timing are not equivalent claims.
Seven-source snapshot is not the future executable build/test dependency closure; toolchain, headers, binary and fixture closure still need independent build and functional gates.
Future real-fixture validation must establish direct C supported counts; wrapper equality alone could be original fallback.
